html:
A huge mosque in Casablanca, Morocco, built from 1986 to 1993, partly on a platform over the Atlantic Ocean. Its minaret, about 210 metres tall, was the tallest in the world until a taller one was built at the Great Mosque of Algiers.

King Hassan II wanted a great monument for Casablanca, Morocco's largest city, and quoted the Quranic verse that God's throne was upon the water. The French architect Michel Pinseau designed it, and thousands of Moroccan craftsmen carved its marble, cedar wood, plaster and zellige tile work. Much of the cost was raised by a public subscription, to which many Moroccans felt pressed to give.

The prayer hall holds some 25,000 people and the courtyard many more. It has a retractable roof, heated floors and a laser on the minaret that points toward Mecca. It is one of the few mosques in Morocco open to non-Muslim visitors.
